meta.title: The Peacock and the Crane
meta.textType: story: a traditional tale told by Grandma

paragraphs: On Saturday, April seventeenth, Dad took Lily, Tom, and Pip to Green Hill. Before lunch, Tom and Lily had a short water fight with two small cups. Pip barked at the drops and ran under the table. The afternoon was hot, but the big tree gave a lot of shade. After lunch, the children sat on a mat under the mango tree. Grandma sat on a low chair next to them, and Pip lay at their feet. Lily showed Grandma her new shiny butterfly hair clip. "Isn't it attractive?" she asked. Grandma smiled. "This story is very old," she said. "Today you will hear the story of the peacock and the crane," she added.

This was Grandma's story. A proud peacock lived in the king's garden. Every morning, he opened his attractive blue and green tail among the flowers. The other birds looked at him, but he did not look at them. He thought, "No bird is as beautiful as I am." One day, a gray crane stopped by the garden pond. She was a foreign bird, and she flew across the wide ocean every year. The peacock saw her and laughed. "What a pity!" he said. "Your feathers have no color at all."

The crane opened her wings and rose into the air. "Your tail is beautiful," she called down, "but I can fly over the hills and see the whole world." "You can only walk in this garden." She flew up over the green hills, and soon she was small and gray in the sky. The peacock stood below and looked up. He closed his tail slowly. The garden was quiet, and the flowers did not move.

That was the end of Grandma's story. The mango tree moved in the wind, and nobody spoke. Tom looked at the hills behind the house. "The peacock seems very quiet now," he said. "Was the crane angry?" asked Lily. "Maybe," said Grandma. "What do you think?" Lily looked at the hills for a long time. Then she touched her hair clip and said nothing.

Dad came from the porch and sat on the mat. "Grandma never gives the end of a story," he told them. "The peacock might not laugh at the next bird," said Tom. "Or he may laugh again tomorrow," said Dad. Grandma smiled and gave each child a slice of mango. Lily took the shiny clip out of her hair and put it in her pocket.
text.summary: At Green Hill, Lily shows Grandma her shiny new hair clip. Grandma tells the old tale of a proud peacock who laughs at a gray crane, and the crane flies away over the hills. Lily thinks about the story, and she says nothing.
